title: Geometry of Straight Lines
summary: Recognise angle pairs formed by intersecting and parallel lines (adjacent, vertically opposite, corresponding, alternate and co-interior angles) and use them, with reasons, to calculate unknown angles.

notes.text: Two angles are **complementary** if they add up to $90^\circ$ (e.g. $37^\circ$ and $53^\circ$). Two angles are **supplementary** if they add up to $180^\circ$ (e.g. $112^\circ$ and $68^\circ$).
**Adjacent** angles share a vertex and a common arm, and lie on opposite sides of that arm (next to each other).
Lines that meet at $90^\circ$ are **perpendicular**. We write $AB \perp CD$.

items: **Angles on a straight line** add up to $180^\circ$. Reason: (∠s on a str line).
**Angles around a point** add up to $360^\circ$. Reason: (∠s round a pt).
**Vertically opposite angles** are equal. Reason: (vert opp ∠s).

notes.svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 300 200" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="15"><g fill="none" stroke="#000" stroke-width="1.5"><line x1="40" y1="40" x2="260" y2="160"/><line x1="40" y1="160" x2="260" y2="40"/></g><g fill="#000" text-anchor="middle"><text x="150" y="80">1</text><text x="184" y="105">2</text><text x="150" y="130">3</text><text x="116" y="105">4</text></g></svg>
notes.caption: Two intersecting lines. Angles 1 and 3 are vertically opposite (equal); so are angles 2 and 4. Adjacent angles such as 1 and 2 lie on a straight line and add up to 180°.

notes.text: **Why are vertically opposite angles equal?** In the diagram, $\hat{1} + \hat{2} = 180^\circ$ and $\hat{2} + \hat{3} = 180^\circ$ (both ∠s on a str line). So $\hat{1} = 180^\circ - \hat{2} = \hat{3}$.

notes.title: Worked example 1
notes.problem:
(a) Angles $x$ and $3x$ lie next to each other on a straight line. Find $x$.
(b) Three angles around a point are $120^\circ$, $95^\circ$ and $y$. Find $y$.
(c) Two lines intersect. One angle is $3x + 10^\circ$ and the vertically opposite angle is $5x - 30^\circ$. Find $x$.
steps: (a) $x + 3x = 180^\circ$ (∠s on a str line), so $4x = 180^\circ$ and $x = 45^\circ$.
(c) $3x + 10^\circ = 5x - 30^\circ$ (vert opp ∠s), so $40^\circ = 2x$ and $x = 20^\circ$. Each angle is $70^\circ$.

notes.text: **Parallel lines** never meet; they are always the same distance apart. On diagrams they are marked with matching arrows, and we write $AB \parallel CD$. A **transversal** is a line that crosses two or more other lines. It forms eight angles, four at each intersection.

notes.caption: AB ∥ CD, cut by a transversal. At the top intersection the angles are a (top right), b (top left), c (bottom left) and d (bottom right); at the bottom intersection they are e, f, g and h in the same positions.
Angle pairs formed by parallel lines (AB ∥ CD in the diagram)
rows: Same position at each intersection (an F shape)
Between the parallel lines, on opposite sides of the transversal (a Z shape)
Between the parallel lines, on the same side of the transversal (a C or U shape)

notes.label: Common mistake
notes.text: These relationships are only true if the lines are **parallel**. If the lines are not parallel, corresponding and alternate angles are not equal. Always include "$AB \parallel CD$" in your reason.

notes.title: Worked example 2
notes.problem: In the diagram, $AB \parallel CD$ and $a = 50^\circ$. Find $b$, $c$, $e$ and $h$, giving reasons.

notes.label: Exam tip
notes.text: In a figure with parallel lines, every angle is either equal to the acute angle or equal to the obtuse angle, and acute + obtuse $= 180^\circ$. Use this to check your answers.

notes.title: Worked example 3: using algebra
notes.problem: Two co-interior angles between parallel lines are $2x + 20^\circ$ and $x + 40^\circ$. Find $x$ and the two angles.

notes.text: The relationships also work in reverse. Two lines cut by a transversal are parallel if **any one** of these is true:

items: a pair of corresponding angles is equal (reason: corresp ∠s =);
a pair of alternate angles is equal (reason: alt ∠s =);
a pair of co-interior angles adds up to $180^\circ$ (reason: co-int ∠s supp).

notes.title: Worked example 4
notes.problem: A transversal cuts lines $PQ$ and $RS$. Two alternate angles are both $72^\circ$. Are $PQ$ and $RS$ parallel?
steps: The alternate angles are equal, so $PQ \parallel RS$ (alt ∠s =).

items: Complementary: add to $90^\circ$. Supplementary: add to $180^\circ$.
Angles on a straight line add to $180^\circ$; angles around a point add to $360^\circ$; vertically opposite angles are equal.
With parallel lines: corresponding angles are equal (F), alternate angles are equal (Z), co-interior angles add to $180^\circ$ (C).
Equal corresponding or alternate angles, or supplementary co-interior angles, prove that lines are parallel.
Always write a reason, and say which lines are parallel.

questions.explanation: An angle between $180^\circ$ and $360^\circ$ is reflex.

questions.prompt: What is the complement of $37^\circ$, in degrees?
What is the supplement of $112^\circ$, in degrees?
Vertically opposite angles add up to $180^\circ$.
questions.explanation: Vertically opposite angles are **equal**. It is adjacent angles on a straight line that add up to $180^\circ$.

questions.prompt: Angles $x$ and $3x$ lie next to each other on a straight line. Calculate $x$, in degrees.
Three angles around a point are $120^\circ$, $95^\circ$ and $y$. Calculate $y$, in degrees.
In the parallel-lines diagram in the notes, what are angles $a$ and $e$ called?
questions.explanation: $a$ and $e$ are both in the top-right position at their intersections: corresponding angles (F shape).

questions.prompt: In the parallel-lines diagram in the notes, what are angles $c$ and $e$ called?
questions.explanation: They are between the parallel lines, on opposite sides of the transversal (Z shape): alternate angles.

questions.prompt: Lines $AB$ and $CD$ are parallel. Two co-interior angles are formed; one of them is $130^\circ$. Calculate the other, in degrees.
questions.explanation: Co-interior angles between parallel lines add to $180^\circ$: $180 - 130 = 50$.

questions.prompt: Match each angle size with its type.
questions.explanation: Acute: less than $90^\circ$; right: $90^\circ$; obtuse: between $90^\circ$ and $180^\circ$; straight: $180^\circ$; revolution: $360^\circ$.

questions.prompt: Co-interior angles between parallel lines add up to $180^\circ$.
questions.explanation: Co-interior angles are supplementary when the lines are parallel.

questions.prompt: What word describes two angles that add up to $90^\circ$?
Two straight lines intersect. One angle is $3x + 10^\circ$ and the vertically opposite angle is $5x - 30^\circ$. Calculate $x$ and the size of the angles.
In the parallel-lines diagram in the notes, $AB \parallel CD$ and $a = 50^\circ$. Calculate $b$, $c$, $e$ and $h$. Give a reason for each.
questions.memo:
$b = 130^\circ$ (∠s on a str line) ✓ (1)
$c = 50^\circ$ (vert opp ∠s) ✓ (1)
$e = 50^\circ$ (corresp ∠s; $AB \parallel CD$) ✓ (1)
$h = 130^\circ$ ($h = d = b$; corresp ∠s and vert opp ∠s) ✓ (1)

questions.prompt: A transversal cuts lines $PQ$ and $RS$. Two alternate angles both measure $72^\circ$. What can you conclude about $PQ$ and $RS$? Give a reason.
questions.memo:
$PQ \parallel RS$ ✓ (1)
Reason: alternate angles are equal (alt ∠s =) ✓ (1)

questions.prompt: Two co-interior angles between parallel lines are $2x + 20^\circ$ and $x + 40^\circ$. Calculate $x$ and the size of each angle.
